1. _______ is the ability to influence others that stems from the leader's desirable traits and
characteristics.
A. Referent power
B. Expert power
C. Coercive power
D. Legitimate power
2. _____ is the ability to inspire confidence and support among the people who are
needed to achieve organizational goals.
A. Stewardship
B. Management
C. Leadership
D. Motivation
3. Entertaining clients, being available to outsiders as an organizational representative,
and escorting official visitors are all behaviors that fit the _____ role of a manager.
A. spokesperson
B. negotiator
C. figurehead
D. coach and mentor
4. When an individual maintains composure when dealing with a crisis we can conclude
that he or she is _______.
A. self-confident
B. trustworthy
C. emotionally stable
D. assertive
5. Two employees cannot agree to compromise. Their manager intervenes. The manager
is filling the role of
A. spokesperson.
B. liaison.
C. disturbance handler.
D. disseminator.
6. Managers today must consider each of the following except
A. diversity.
B. stagnation.
C. changes in technology.
D. changes in organization flexibility.
7. Which of the following is not an assumption of Theory X?

A. People do not like to work.
B. Managers have to control and coerce employees.
C. People are ambitious.
D. People prefer to avoid responsibility.
8. Leadership is a function of:
A. Manager, leader and follower
B. Manager, leader and situation
C. Manager, Follower and situation
D. Leader, Follower and situation
9. The administrative assistant for the president of Lever Brothers of Pakistan has held
that job for thirty-five years. When the staff needs to accomplish a task, they often get her
advice. She has which power?
A. Expert
B. Reward
C. Legitimate
D. Coercive
10. MR. Zeshan, Manager Bata Pakistan is primarily concerned with efficiency and
performance of his subordinates. According to the Michigan studies he exhibits which
leader behavior?
A. Job-centered
B. Employee-centered
C. Initiating-structure
D. Consideration
Q#1. Managing resistance to change that is _____ is extremely challenging.
a. passive
b. resolute
c. deferred
d. explicit
Q#2. All of the following are sources of organizational resistance to change
except:
a. structural inertia
b. security
c. limited focus of change
d. threat to established power relationships
Q#3. Conflict is functional if it _____.

a. is accepted by all members of a group
b. is satisfying to the individual members of the group
c. causes group members to argue
d. none of the above
Q#4 Which is not a weakness of group decision making?
a. It is time consuming.
b. There is less originality.
c. It suffers from ambiguous responsibility.
d. It can be dominated by one or a few members.
Q#5. What is brainstorming?
a. a technique used to build group cohesiveness
b. a technique that tends to restrict independent thinking
c. a process for generating ideas
d. a process used mainly when group members cannot agree on a
Q#6. When employees are required to follow their job description or to
comply
with company policies, communication is performing a(n) ______ function.
a. control
b. motivation
c. emotional expression
d. information
Q#7. The product of a sender’s encoding is the _____.
a. channel
b. message
c. transmission
d. medium
Q#8. Which of the following is not true?
a. Theory Y aligns with the participative management style.
b. Employee involvement programs provide intrinsic motivation.
c. Theory X aligns with the autocratic management style.
d. Employee involvement is incompatible with ERG theory.
Q#9. Two managers are talking about how they get the best out of their
employees:

Ali: “I tell my employees that times are tough and there is no way of telling
when
the guys in head office might try to downsize. Let me tell you, a bit of fear
keeps
them focused on the task at hand.”
Shahid “I tell them that head office is making them more responsible for
deciding
how to do their work. The increased sense of ownership they have makes
productivity go way up”
How would these managers be best characterized by Douglas Macgregor?
a. Both hold Theory X assumptions
b. Both hold Theory Y assumptions
c. Shahid holds Theory X assumptions, Ali holds Theory Y assumptions
d. Ali holds Theory X assumptions, Shahid holds Theory Y
assumptions
Q#10. Which of the following is not an example of upward
communication?
a. performance reports prepared by lower management for top
management review
b. informing employees of policies
c. suggestion boxes
d. grievance procedures
Q#1. Which of the following statements about personality is correct?
a. Personality is always stable.
b. Personality is a part of a person.
c. Personality is an aggregate whole.
d. Personality is for the most part comprised of traits that cannot be
measured.

entrepreneurial. Candidates for this position would ideally have what
classification on the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator?
a. INTJs
b. ESTJs

c. ENTPs
d. ISFPs

a. results in a level of effort
b. intensifies an individual’s efforts

a. reactance, congruence and circumstance
b. interest, activity and reward
c. awareness, effort and outcome
d. intensity, direction and persistence

one of those levels?
a. safety needs
b. social needs
c. animal needs
d. self-actualization needs
Q#6. Hunger, thirst, sex, pay, and physical work environment are examples

which of Alderfer’s needs?
a. existence
b. safety

d. physiological

a. seeking responsibility
b. needing to be coerced to achieve goals
c. viewing work as a normal daily activity
d. exercising self control

a. Theories X and Y
b. Motivator-Hygiene Theory

c. Hierarchy of Needs Theory
d. Satisfaction/Dissatisfaction Theory

ENG509 Lesson (20~36) Extracted from slides

   MORPHOLOGY AND SYTANX
         (ENG509)

         Prepared By: Sajid Iqbal & Saira Hafeez

VIRTUAL UNIVERSITY OF PAKISTAN

                                                   1

                  ENG509 Lesson (20~36) Extracted from slides

➢ If an animal is innately programmed for some type of behaviour, then there are likely to be
  biological clues. (Mean something innate that is responsible for some particular behaviour, in
  linguistics we are searching for some innate thing which is responsible for language speaking)

➢ Fish have bodies which are streamlined and smooth, with fins and a powerful tail structurally
  adapted for moving fast through the water. (Body structure and physical behaviour of fish have
  resemblance)

➢ Biological clues are not essential. It is impossible to guess their behaviour from their bodies solely.
  (But these biological clues have some relevance)

➢ Birds make nests, and, sometimes, animals behave in a way quite contrary to what might be
  expected from their physical form.

➢ Changes in the form of the body or structural changes are the most direct indications of innate
  programming.

➢ Physiological adaptations include changes in the bodily functions, such as rate of heartbeat and
  breathing.

➢ If we look at the organs used in speech, humans seem to be somewhere in the middle between the
  obvious structural adaptation of birds to flying, and the apparent lack of correlation between birds
  and nest building.

➢ The human brain and vocal tract have a number of slightly unusual features which can not indicate
  sufficiently that people can talk. (Can be assumed by some analysis)

➢ If we assume that all humans speak a language, then biological facts can be viewed as partial
  adaptations of the body to the production of language.

➢ Another important difference between humans and monkeys concerns the larynx, which contains the
  ‘voice box’ or ‘vocal cords simpler in structure than that of other primates.

➢ This is an advantage as air can move freely past and then out through the nose and mouth
  without being hindered by other appendages. (As we have studied that human children and
  chimpanzees have same larynx so that they can drink and breathe together i.e. an infant sucking her
  mother)

➢ Human brain is very different in appearance from that of other animals.

                                                                                                       2

                  ENG509 Lesson (20~36) Extracted from slides

➢ Human brain is heavier than animals

➢ Human brain with more surface folding of the cortex, outer layer of ‘grey matter’ which surrounds
  the inner core of nerve fibres.

➢ In human brain, though grey matter is actually pink in live humans, it goes grey after death.

➢ Superficially, the brains of a chimp and a human have certain similarities.

➢ Language emerges at about the same time in children all over the world.

➢ Children normally begin to speak between their eighteenth and twenty-eighth months.

➢ It is suggested that language may be set in motion by a biological clock, similar to the one which
  causes kittens to open their eyes when they are a few days old.

➢ Behaviour that is triggered off biologically has a number of special characteristics.

➢ If it can be shown that speech, like sexual activities and the ability to walk, falls into the category of
  biologically scheduled behaviour.

➢ The behaviour emerges before it is necessary

➢ Appearance of behaviour is not the result of a conscious decision.

➢ Emergence of behaviour is not triggered by external events (though the surrounding environment
  must be sufficiently ‘rich’ for it to develop adequately).

➢ There is a regular sequence of ‘milestones’ as the behaviour develops, and these can usually be
  correlated with age and other aspects of development.

➢ There may be a ‘critical period’ for the acquisition of the behaviour.

➢ Direct teaching and intensive practice have relatively little effect.

➢ Although children differ enormously in their ability to knit or play the violin, their language
  proficiency varies to a much lesser extent.

➢ Children acquire language without making any conscious decision about it.

                                                                                                          3

                  ENG509 Lesson (20~36) Extracted from slides

➢ Children begin to talk even when their surroundings remain unchanged.

➢ Most of them live in the same house, eat the same food, have the same parents, and follow the same
  routine. No specific event or feature in their surroundings suddenly starts them off talking.

➢ Children do not manufacture any new brain cells after birth.

➢ They are born with millions, perhaps billions. At first the cells are not all interconnected, and the
  brain is relatively light (about 300g).

➢ From birth to around 2 years, many more cells interconnect, and brain weight increases rapidly. By
  the age of 2, it weighs nearly 1000g (Lenneberg1967).

➢ Although no external event causes the behaviour, the surrounding environment must be
  sufficiently ‘rich ‘for it to develop adequately.

➢ ‘Direct teaching and intensive practice have relatively little effect.’

➢ In activities such as typing or playing tennis, a person’s achievement is often directly related to the
  amount of teaching they receive and the hours of practice they put in. Not ‘naturally’ superb athletes
  can win.

➢ We may conclude, then, that mere practice – in the sense of direct repetition and imitation – does not
  affect the acquisition of language in a significant way

                                                     Lecture: 21

Content-Based Instruction

It is the teaching of content or information in the language being learned with little or no direct effort to teach the
language separately from the content being taught.

Principles of Content-Based Instruction

    1. Content-Based Instruction better reflects learners' needs for learning a second language
    2. People learn a second language more successfully when they use the language as a means of acquiring
       information, rather than mastering the language for its own sake.

Assumptions of Content-Based Instruction

    1. Language is purposeful
       Role of language as a vehicle for learning content entails the centrality of linguistic entities longer than single
       sentences, because the focus of teaching is how meanings are constructed and communicated through texts and
       discourse.
    2. Language is text and discourse-based
       In a content-based class, students are often involved in activities that link the skills. Hence, students might read
       and take notes, listen and write a summary, or respond orally.
    3. Language use draws on integrated skills
       Language is used for specific purposes. The purpose may be academic, vocational, social, or recreational but
       it gives direction, shape, and ultimately meaning to discourse and texts
    4. Students learn best when instruction addresses students' needs
    5. Teaching builds on the previous experience of the learners

Student goals of an immersion program include
(1) Developing a high level of proficiency in the FL

(2) Developing positive attitudes toward foreign language speakers and their culture(s)

(3) Developing English language skills commensurate with expectations for a student's age and abilities

(4) Gaining designated skills and knowledge in the content areas of the curriculum

Immigrant On-Arrival Programs - focus on the newly arrived immigrants in a country and their need for survival.
Such learners typically need to learn how to deal with differing kinds of real-world content as a basis for social survival.

Students with Limited English Proficiency (SLEP) programs – these are governmentally mandated programs to serve
especially those children whose parents might be served by the on-arrival programs, but more generally designed to
provide in-class instruction to those whose language competence is insufficient to participate fully in normal school
instruction.

Language for Specific Purposes (LSP) - a movement that seeks to serve the language needs of learners who need
language in order to carry out specific roles (e.g., student, engineer, technician, and nurse) rather than master the
language for its own sake.

LSP/EST subfields

       ESP (English for Specific Purposes)
       EOP (English for Occupational Purposes)
       EAP (English for Academic Purposes)

Pronunciation - the articulation of individual sounds and the distinctive features of sounds like voicing, aspiration,
stress and intonation.

Phonological loop - the brain saying a word or phrase over and over to itself in order to keep it in working memory or
to help it move into long-term memory.

Criteria to typify a good pronunciation

    1.   Intelligibility
    2.   Identity
    3.   Ease of learning
    4.   Acceptability by parents and the educational administration
    5.   Availability of teachers and materials to support the wanted pronunciation

Nativeness principle - sets a native-speaker goal for learners

Intelligibility principle - accepts accents and sets understanding as the goal

Factors Affecting the Learning of another Sound System

Learners’

    1.   Age
    2.   First language
    3.   Current stage of proficiency development
    4.   The experience and attitudes
    5.   The conditions for teaching and learning

Competing explanations of the cause of the relationship b/w age and accent

Physical explanation - there are physical changes in the brain as a result of age that affect the learning of a new sound
system and other aspects of the language.

Intellectual explanation - learners have already learned the sound system of their first language and this increasingly
disrupts their perception of a second language.

Psychological explanation - pronunciation is a part of our personality and as we become older we become more
protective of our personality and unwilling to change it.

Three reasons why learners might have difficulty in learning new sounds

    1. They overlook some feature
    2. The learners sound bad to themselves when they copy well
    3. The learners become anxious about making the sounds

Learning New Sounds: A Procedure

Before teaching or correcting a sound, certain information is needed. Then the teacher can follow several steps to teach
the sound.

Necessary Information:

        Does the learner have the wanted sound in the first language? What is the nearest sound?
        What sound does the learner put in place of the wanted sound?
        Does the learner make this mistake in initial, middle, and final position?
        What is the difference between the wanted sound and the unwanted sound?

Teaching the Sound

Teach the learner to hear the wanted sound by using distinguishing and identifying activities. Distinguishing should
come before identifying.

Slurring and bracketing

In slurring, the tongue or another part of the mouth is slowly moved from one position to another. This is done several
times with the learners copying the teacher. Then the movement is stopped a part of the way between the two sounds so
that the wanted sound is produced.

Assessing Reading

1- Reading Aloud

        Reading aloud can be used to check the learner’s skill at word recognition

Four ways of scoring the cloze test

Issues in Making and Using Reading Comprehension Tests

        Should learners be allowed to use dictionaries?

Principles for Teaching Writing

Meaning-focused Input

        Learners should be prepared before what they are going to write
        Learners should bring experience and knowledge to their writing

Meaning-focused Output

        Learners should write with a message-focused purpose
        Learners should use writing to increase their language knowledge
        Writing instruction should be based on a careful needs analysis

Language-focused Learning

        Learners should know about the parts of the writing process
        Learners should know about the strategies for dealing with parts of the writing process
        Learners should be aware of the ethical issues involved in writing

Fluency Development

Designing Tasks

Four kinds of tasks

   1) Experience tasks try to narrow the gap as much as possible by using or developing learners’ previous experience
   2) Shared tasks try to get learners to help each other cross the gap
   3) Guided tasks try to bridge the gap by providing the support of exercises
   4) Independent tasks leave learners to rely on their own resources

Ways of making sure learners have the experience needed to do a particular task

1- Control through selection

        Using simplified material
        Using graded material
        Using learner’s L1 material
        Using learner’s produced material

2- Recalling prior experience

        Brainstorming
        Discussions

3- Pre-teaching or experiencing

        Visits and field trips
        Direct teaching of content

Experience tasks for writing

       Draw and write - the learners draw a picture about something that happened to them or something imagined,
        and then they write about it.
       Linked skills - the writing task is set as the final activity in a series that involves speaking about, then listening
        to and then reading about the topic and then writing.
       Ten perfect sentences - the teacher showing the learners a picture and the learners must write ten separate
        sentences about that.
       Partial writing - working together the learners list useful words that they will need in the following writing task
       Setting your own questions - Each student produces the question they want to write about. After translating in
        Standard English, it is taken as an examination question which the students answer under examination conditions.

                                                       Lecture: 25

Shared tasks have the advantages of:

        Requiring little preparation by the teacher
        Reducing the teacher’s supervision
        Encouraging the learners to see each other as a learning resource

Reproduction exercise / dicto-comp

It is half-way between dictation and composition. Here, the learners read or listen to a story and then they retell it without
looking at the original.

The exercise can be made more difficult to suit the abilities of the learners. Here are three different ways of doing this,
the second way is more difficult than the first, and the third is more difficult than the second.

Collaboration - a process in which two or more learners need to work together to achieve a common goal, usually the
completion of a task.

Collaboration puts learners into a semi-autonomous situation in which they are faced with a task, question or problem
and must use discourse to negotiate each participant’s separate learning strategies and make joint decisions about what
is (and is not) worth investigating and learning.

The place of collaboration in CALL

Collaboration is an important activity in the classroom because it encourages both social skills and thinking skills and
mirrors the way in which learners often need to work in an academic setting and certainly once they leave it.

Types of goal structure

  1) Individualistic - where a learner believes his or her chances of reaching the goal are unrelated to what others do
  2) Competitive - where a learner believes he or she can reach the goal only when others cannot
  3) Cooperative - where a learner believes that he or she can reach the goal only if others can too

Scaffolding describes a situation in which a learner interacts with someone who can guide, support, and shape his or
her learning; in CALL the computer can sometimes take on these functions.

Structuring Collaboration

The teacher must structure collaboration at computers through:

    1.   Establishing students’ mixed-ability teams
    2.   Establishing positive interdependence
    3.   Insuring individual accountability
    4.   Teaching cooperative social skills
    5.   Helping groups process information

Interdependence in collaboration

1 Goal interdependence – stating clearly what each member of the group should know how to complete the task

2 Task interdependence – clearly defining the group goal, and what the team should be able to produce

3 Resource interdependence – specifying parameters, materials, the team’s task

4 Role interdependence – reviewing the individual roles for the group members: keyboarder, checker, reporter,
summarizer.

Cooperative learning is an activity set by the teacher or is merely a mode of instruction.

Collaborative activities are ones spontaneously set up by the learners or whereby learners have greater control over the
design of their learning.

Reasons for people to collaborate Argyle

    1. For external rewards
    2. To form and further relationships
    3. To share activities they are involved in

Backward Design

This curriculum approach begins with a specification of learning outputs and to use these as the basis for developing
instructional processes and input. Backward design starts with a careful statement of the desired results or outcomes:
appropriate teaching activities and content are derived from the very results of learning. It is also known as ends-means’
approach.

       Step 1: Diagnosis of needs
       Step 2: Formulation of objectives
       Step 3: Selection of content
       Step 4: Organization of content
       Step 5: Selection of learning experiences
       Step 6: Organization of learning experiences
       Step 7: Determination of what to evaluate and of the ways of doing it

There steps in Backward Design approach by Wiggins and McTighe

Competency-Based Instruction within Backward Design Approach

The process consisted of:

       Needs analysis
       Identify topics for the survival curriculum (e.g. banking, health, shopping).
       Identify target tasks, design tasks.

Subject-centered Design

The main focus is on curriculum development (not human development) with subject specialists developing ―high
standards‖ for student uniformity. The main goal and purpose is to standardize students, to make them alike with a ―
core curriculum.

Learner-centered Design

This approach places the learner at the center of the pedagogic process and sees education not as a matter of receiving
information but of intelligent inquiry and thought.

A learner-centered curriculum will contain similar elements to those contained in traditional curriculum development,
that is, planning (including needs analysis, goal and objective setting), implementation (including methodology and
material development) and evaluation. However, the main difference between learner centered and traditional
curriculum development is that in the former the curriculum is a collaborative effort between teachers and learners.

Creating Fixed-Choice Test Items: Matching Exercises

Matching test items are also selection items specially used to measure a student's ability to identify the relationship
between a set of similar items, each of which has two components.

Advantages Matching Exercises

       Ease of construction
       Measure a large amount of related factual material in a relatively short time

Limitations of Matching Exercises

       Restricted to the measurement of factual information
       Highly susceptible to the presence of irrelevant clues
       Difficulty of findings homogenous material

                                                    Lecture: 24

Suggestions for Constructing Matching Exercises

       Use only homogeneous material in the single matching exercise
       Include an unequal number of responses and premises
       Arrange the list of responses in logical order
       Indicate the directions the basis for matching the responses

Forms of Supply Type

       Short answers
       Completion items

They only differ in form of presentation. Short answers are presented in the form of direct questions while completion
items are incomplete statements.

Both of them can be answered with a word, phrase, number, or symbol.

Advantages of Short Answer/Completion Questions

       Teacher wants to control the possibility of guessing
       Teacher wants students to complete a large number of items in a fairly short time
       The possibility of guessing the correct answers to these questions is greatly reduced when compared with true-
        false questions

Disadvantages

       Difficult to frame questions for one specific answer
       Not usable to measure complex learning outcomes

Suggestions for Constructing Short Answer/Completion Questions

Constructed Response Test Items

Subjective test items (essay questions) are constructed response type questions that can be the best way to measure the
students' higher order thinking skills. Such as applying, organizing, synthesizing, integrating, evaluating, or projecting.

Essay type questions are divided into two types

    1. Restricted Response Items
    2. Extended Response Items

Examples:

        Analysis of relationship.
        Compare and contrast positions.
        Explain cause-effect relationship

Guidelines for Constructing Restricted Response Essay Type Items

        Prepare a tentative scoring key in advance
        Do not employ optional questions
        Verify a question‘s quality by writing a trial response to the question
        Evaluate essay responses anonymously
        Specify the value and an approximate time limit for each question

                                                      Lecture: 29

Advantages of essay type items (Extended response questions)

        Effective for assessing higher order abilities
        Comparatively less time consuming
        Emphasizes essential communications skills

Scoring Rubrics provide two benefits

        They support the examination to the extent to which the specified criteria has been reached.
        They provide feedback to students concerning how to improve their performance

Types of Scoring Rubrics

        The analytic (scoring key, point or rating) method
          The analytic scoring requires developing a list of major elements that students are expected to include in an
            ideal answer of a question
          Decide the number of points awarded to students when they include each element
          When assigning number to each element, be sure the total points should match with the essay‘s total value
        The holistic (also called global, sorting or rating) method
          The holistic scoring rubric requires making a judgment about the overall quality of each student‘s response
            to an item.
          No need to mark each specific content element that a student included in the answer.

                                                      Lecture: 30

Item Analysis

It reveals if an item is:

                                                                                                                   3
                                                                                                         ENG520...…….
       Too easy
       Too difficult
       Failing to show a difference between skilled and unskilled examinees

The two most common statistics reported in Item Analysis

    1. Item difficulty (which is a measure of the proportion of examinees who responded to an item correctly)
    2. Item discrimination (which is a measure of how well the item discriminates between examinees who are
       knowledgeable in the content area and those who are not).

Distractor analysis - provides a measure of how well each of the incorrect options contributes to the quality of a
multiple choice item.

Appropriate Time for Item Analysis

    1. After administration, but before scoring – it helps the test developers identify errors in the scoring key or defects

ALINK v1.6 is copyright 1998/9 Anthony A.J. Williams. All Rights Reserved.

ALINK is a linker for OBJ and LIB files, and generates MSDOS COM and
MSDOS EXE files, and Win32 PE files. Win32 resource files are also supported
for linking to PE files. MS/Intel OMF and MS-COFF object and library files
are supported. MS-COFF import libraries are not supported, and will cause
an undefined symbol error in a .idata section.

ALINK is free, and as such there is no warranty whatsoever. If anything bad
happens, it is entirely your responsibility.

The command line is:

ALINK [options] filename [options] [filenames] [options] ...

By default ALINK performs a case-sensitive link to an EXE file, without
padding segments. If filenames don't include an extension, .obj is assumed.
Additional parameters can be taken from response files, by specifying a
filename preceded by an @ sign, e.g.

ALINK @response.fil

Blanks lines are ignored, options may be specified together, or on separate
lines. Quoted strings are treated as a single parameter.
Semicolons are treated as the start of a comment, and the rest of the
line will be ignored. If you really want a semicolon, enclose it in
quotes.
Options and filenames can be used in the parameter file, but filenames may
not include wildcards. Multiple response files can be referenced, and
additional response files may be included from within a response file.
Cyclic references are not detected, and will cause the program
to loop until it runs out of memory (never, if the response files don't
contain any options!).

Possible options are:

-c      Enable Case sensitive link
-c+     "
-c-     Disable Case sensitive link
-p      Pad segments (initialise all segments)
-p+     "
-p-     Disable segment padding
-o yyy  yyy is output filename
-oxxx   xxx specifies output format
        COM = output COM file
        EXE = output EXE file
        PE  = output Win32 PE file (.EXE)
-m      Generate map file
-m+     "
-m-     Don't generate map file
-L ddd  Add directory ddd to library search list
-h      Display this help list
-H      "
-?      "
-entry name  Use public symbol name as the entry point

In addition, for PE files the following options apply:

-base addr           Set Image Base (default=4Mb)
-objectalign xxx     Set section alignment in memory (default=64K)
-filealign xxx       Set section alignment in file (default=512)
-subsys xxx          Set windows subsystem to use (default=windows)
                     windows, win or gui => windows subsystem
                     console, con or char => console subsystem
                     native => native subsystem
                     posix => POSIX subsystem
-subsysver x.y       Set subsystem version x.y (default=4.0)
-osver x.y           Set OS version x.y (default=1.0)
-heapsize xxx        Set heap size (default=1Mb)
-heapcommitsize xxx  Set heap commit size (default=4K)
-stacksize xxx       Set stack size (default=1Mb)
-stackcommitsize xxx Set stack commit size (default=4K)
-dll                 Build a DLL instead of an EXE file.
-stub filename       Use the specified file as the MSDOS stub.

Note that Windows 3.1=> ver 3.10, 3.5=>ver 3.50
If you type -subsysver 3.1, this is the same as 3.01

The alignments must be powers of 2. ObjectAlign can be 512 to 256Mb, FileAlign can
be 512 to 64K. The Image base and alignments can be specified as decimal numbers, or as
hex numbers prefixed by 0x (in fact, any number format supported by the C function
strtoul). The image base must be a multiple of 64K.

options are case sensitive, so -ocom is invalid, as is -C.

If an output filename is not specified, then the output file is determined
from the output type, and the root of the first object file.

e.g.

        ALINK file1.obj -oCOM -o outfile.com

        Generates outfile.com from file1.obj

        ALINK file2.obj file3.obj -oEXE

        Generates file2.exe

Segments from different object files are combined if they have the same name
and class, and are not declared private. Absolute segments are never
combined, and stack segments are always combined.

Segments are emitted in the order they are present in the object files,
unless groups are used. All segments in groups are emitted before segments
not in groups. A segment may not be in more than one group. Segments in groups
are emitted in the order specified in the group definition. If two different
definitions of the same group specify different orders, the first definition
is used.

Thus, if in the second example above, file2.obj contains a group definition
equivalent to

        agroup group code,data,stack

and file3.obj contains a group definition equivalent to

        agroup group data,stack,bss,code

The final output for agroup will be

        code,data,stack,bss

The text output from the linker is quite verbose, and lists all the files as
they are loaded in. Any unrecognised object records will cause an error. Any
recognised, but ignored records, such as LINNUM records and COMENT records
will be printed on the screen. Since debug information is often contained in
COMENT records, this could lead to a lot of output.

The map file will list the segments, publics, imports and exports.

A sample Import library for Win32 is included as win32.lib. All named exports in
Kernel32, User32, GDI32, Shell32, ADVAPI32, version,winmm, lz32,commdlg and commctl
are included. Use

alink -oPE file[.obj] win32.lib to include it.

or specify

INCLUDELIB "win32"

in your source file (TASM)

This consists of a series of entries for import redirection - call
MessageBoxA, and it jumps to [__imp_MessageBoxA], which is in the Import
Table.

Thus calls to imports will run faster if call [__imp_importName] is used
instead of call importName.

See test.asm, my sample program, which calls up a message box both ways.

See rtn.asm for an example program using NASM, and resources.

anthony_w@geocities.com

“B.S English Applied
 Linguistics Project
    Guidelines”

   “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

     What is a Research Project or Thesis?

 Thesis or project is a research work in which you’ll be
provided with a topic by your instructor and you’ve to do
                  research on that topic.
Your work should be plagiarism free in order to pass that
specific project course because it’s mandatory for degree
                        completion.

              “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

     Components of the Project/Thesis

  Thesis/Project comprised of mainly five chapters:

1. Introduction          2. Literature Review
3. Research Methodology
4. Results and Discussion
5. Findings/conclusion/Recommendations

          “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

                   1. Introduction
In the introduction chapter, you’ll write a brief
introduction of the topic assigned to you by the
instructor. You can get idea from the previous research
articles but you can’t take material from those articles
because that will make your work plagiarized and you’ll
get 0 marks in that assignment.

           “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

Your first assignment will be about the introduction chapter and will include the
                                 following headings:
                                  1.1 Introduction
                write an introduction of the topic (2 pages almost)
                            1.2: Objectives of the study
     you’ll write the objectives of your study by using the words like “ to
                  investigate…, to explore…, to highlight..etc.
              you can add 1-2 objectives about your research study.
Example: To investigate the role of First language on the English speaking skills
                                      of students.
                              1.3: Research Questions
Add 1-2 research questions by using the question words e.g. what, how, why, etc.
 Example: What is the Role of L1 on the English speaking skills of the students.
             (Note: It’s just an example. Your topic will be different.)

                    “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

                 1.4: Statement of the problem
 Under this sub-heading, you’ll write a short paragraph of about
200 words about the problem that you’re going to discuss in your
                         research study.
                 1.5: Significance of the study
  In this sub-heading, you’ve to write a paragraph of 200-300
  words about the significance/importance of the topic for the
          audience (teachers, students, local people, etc)

                “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

          Chapter 2: Literature Review
This is the second chapter of your thesis and you’ve to write
this in your 2nd assignment after the approval of your 1st
assignment which was about the introduction.
Literature Review generally means “ the review of the previous
studies that has been done on that specific topic you’re
assigned with.
You’ve to read about 4-5 articles after downloading from the
Google, Google scholar. I’ll prefer Google Scholar because you
can easily get references as well from the Google scholar.
             “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

              Read and open the notepad with your PDF.
   Read the Abstract, methodology and conclusion section of the
   articles you’re reading and write these three sections in a short
              paragraph about 100 words for one article.
(Note: Write the literature review in your own words without using
 the same words as used in the article otherwise your work will be
                              plagiarized.)
Also write the name of the researcher before starting the review of
            the articles e.g. Moyer (2014) investigated ....
 Read 4-5 articles in the same way and write their reviews in your
                               own words.
This is the work you’ve to done in the literature review chapter and
              this chapter should be less than 800 words.
                “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

            Chapter 3: Research Methodology

    This chapter is mostly included in the 2nd assignment with
literature review for Eng528 project but mostly for eng 525,526,
 this chapter is written as a separate one. Whatever it’s place is,
                 the method and formatting is same.
              It includes the following sub-headings:
         3.1: Research Design 3.2: Research Method
        3.3: Population of the study       3.4: Sample size
      3.5: Sampling Technique 3.6: Research instruments
             3.7: Reliability and validity of the tools
                “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

First of all just design survey questionnaires which should include a
maximum of 20 questions and decide what type of research design
you’ll choose in order to collect data e.g. your research method will
  be qualitative or quantitative? You will collect data from online
  survey design or by physically visiting the schools or colleges?
                     After deciding the above factors,
                  select the population and sample size.
E.g. Students of Punjab Group of Colleges will be your population
           and the number of students (100,200) will be the
                         sample size of the study.
         In the Methodology chapter, you just have to design
     questionnaires about your topic, select the research design,
                    population, size and instruments.
                 “Project Guidelines by Maira Shahzadi”

            Chapter 4: Results and Discussion
In this assignment, you’ve to distribute the questionnaires to the
students whether through online survey forms or by taking prints
 of the questionnaire and hand over to the students by physically
                visiting them in school or college.
  After you got your data, analyze it and write it in the form of
                         tables and charts.

      3. Collision induced dissociation

match score

Ans: Agilent ----- Bruker ----- ABI ----- Micromass ----- Waters ----- Shimadzu

Ans: 1) Nominal Mass          2)Monoisotopic Mass        3) Average Mass
Q. Differentiate between polar and non polar amino acids?
Ans: Non polar amino acids:

By Cr. SABA ALWI

Non polar amino acids are hydrophobic in nature. They are mostly found inside of
folded protein.H and C introduce very little dipole movement. e.g Phe, Ala, Leo,
Val etc.
Polar amino acids:
These amino acids are polar but are not charged. Prefer to reside or interact to
aqueous environment. Mostly found at surface of folded protein. E.g Cys, Gly, Ser,
Thr, Tyr etc.

Q. What is meant by “PK” value of an amino acid?
Ans: PK is the value for an amino acid is that PH at which exactly half of amino
acids are charged and half are not charged.

Ans: solubility and reactivity are the key factors that are participating in protein
folding.

Ans: amino acids has unique set of properties such as charge state, polarity and
hydrophobicity.

Ans: 1. Edman degradation
     2. tandem mass spectrometry

configurations • Loops are mostly located on the surface of proteins • Loops are
more “acceptable" of mutations • Loops are flexible & can adopt multiple
conformations • Loops tend to have charged and polar amino acids • Loops are
frequently components of active sites

Ans: Angstrom is a unit of length   equal to 10−10 m (one tenbillionth of a
meter) or 0.1nm .

E-commerce Management

Topics: 1 to 50

    1. What is E-Business?
The term electronic Business or e-business referred to the electronic exchange of information / data or documents both within the organization and with external resources to support business process. E-Business is an umbrella activity of moving from physical file storage to computer storage with the purpose of making business process more efficient. With efficiency comes improved business performance due to low cost of managing business processes. E-business includes vendor communication, order processing, e-procurement, supply chain and other business areas. Interestingly Online Transfer of Payments is part of E-Business also.
The electronic storage of data not only helped in improving the volume/speed of data storage but it also improved the pace of processing and sharing information with the relevant stakeholders ultimately improving business decision making.
E-Business also followed natural adoption process though its inception and this is explained in the image below:

It went from a completely non-existent business model with no defined processes to an era where e-business has become essential for more profitable business. It has transformed and evolved over time to a stage where the products are not only customized but designed by the customers around the globe. Translating the above Natural Evolution into E-Business Evolution:

And what E-Business looks like today??

    2. What is E-Commerce?
E-commerce is the activity focusing specifically on online buying and selling of the products. Being narrower in scope, e-commerce is more concentrated towards buying and selling of the products instead of business processes. Some E-commerce experts also include pre and post sales activities in the scope of e-commerce as well. E-commerce includes transaction among Business-to-Business (B2B), Business-to-Consumer (B2C) and Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C)
 This is how e-commerce works:

    1. A customer tries to order online and his browser communicate with the store web server
    2. Web server sends the order to the order manager
    3. The order manager forward the query to database to check the availability of the product
    4. If the item is not in stock, customer is informed and system may go ahead to order supplies
    5. The database confirms that the product is available
    6. Order manager communicates with merchant system to take payment
    7. Merchant system communicates with bank system for payment processing
    8. Bank system confirm that the customers has enough funds to buy the product
    9. The merchant system gives a go ahead to the transaction
    10. The order manager confirm the success of the transaction
    11. The web server shows the customer that the order has been processed
    12. The order manager send request to warehouse to dispatch product
    13. Delivery vehicle collects the product from warehouse and deliver
    14. The warehouse system sends and email to customer to tell that the product is on the way
    15. The goods are delivered to customer

    3. Difference between E-Commerce and E-Business
These two terms are used interchangeably but in real these are total opposite of each other. E-Business is superset and E-Commerce is subset from functionality viewpoint. Make it simpler, e-business is wider in scope and its focus in on all business processes conducted online. On the other side, e-commerce is narrower in scope and its main focus is buying and selling only. For example, email marketing to existing and prospective customer is E-Business; technology here is being used as an enabler while growth in revenue totally via Internet is E-Commerce (like Alibaba which uses email marketing too).

    4. Motivation for E-Commerce
E-commerce today is the buzz word in the business and offers very promising benefits in terms of business growth, profit maximization, business reach and reaching international boundaries. Growth of e-commerce is staggering and in 2017 it touched $2.1 Trillion. In US alone, it is 10% of the total retail payment and mobile payments accounted for 11% of the total online shopping. The graph below shows the increasing trend of the online sales.




E-Commerce is not limited to the Western world or the US only. Here are top 10 e-commerce markets in the world.

Analytics and trends related to online shopping shows that people purchases beyond their boundaries and this is where Future Prospects Lies.

    5. Sell-Side E-Commerce: Transactional E-Commerce
The main focus of the sell side e-commerce website is the enable sale of product, either offline or online. Another major intent is to provide information related to the product(s) to the customers but the main business contribution of such sites is through sale of the product. Few examples would be:
    1. www.amazon.com
    2. www.mercedes-benz.com/en/
Amazon is a perfect example of sell side transactional e-commerce that provide customers information related to the products and at the same time it enables them to purchase the product they want.
    6. Sell – Side E-Commerce: Service Oriented Relationship Building Websites
Another type of sell side e-commerce websites are service oriented and relationship building websites. Their major purpose is to provide information to all the customers in order to promote the business. The information is disseminated usually through newsletter and emails. Leads are generated first through these websites followed by sales. These websites are also very effective in identifying potential customers. Website of EY, Ernst & Young (www.ey.com), is a perfect example. EY is the world’s 3rd most largest and successful accounting firm in the world. They don’t sell anything online but they generate potential customer by showcasing their success.
    7. Sell – Side E-Commerce: Brand – Building Websites

115. Payment Gateway in Pakistan: What is Payment Gateway
Payment Gateway helps clients (End users) to directly transfer amount into vendor account. This payment gateway does not work under the ownership of online store rather this service is provided to the vendor by a bank or payment processor. Vendor can link their bank account with the payment gateway and the money from the end user is transferred to their linked account. Payment Gateway is integrated into Online Store. The whole process is shown below:

    116. Payment Gateway in Pakistan - Making Online Payment in Pakistan
Receiving and sending Online Payments is major concern and unfortunately Pakistan does not have its own home grown Payment Gateway. Cash on Delivery is largest source of receiving payment and solutions like Western Union does not transfer amount into Bank Accounts. But the development of the payment gateway in is process and Telecom Companies like Zong, Telenor and Jazz have developed their payment solution to receive money into Bank Account. Banks are not lagging behind and HBL has provided Internet Payment Gateway Solution to be integrated into E-Commerce shop. Using Service like Skrill or Payoneer are helping companies and individuals to receive online payment and withdraw it through ATM’s
    117. Payment Gateway - What is PayPal?
Confinity was founded by Max Levchin, Peter Thiel and Luke Nosek in 1998 and x.com was launched in 1999 by Elon Musk and that ultimately merged with Confinity to launch Paypal in same year. Paypal is world largest payment processor to send and receive money and that enable individuals and Businesses to transfer money electronically. It operates in 202 countries and has 237 million customers. PayPal is not a Bank because it does not give loan but money can be withdrawn without bank account.
    118. Payment Gateway - How it Work
Paypal is like Digital Wallet with different payment options. Credit Cards, Debit Card, Master Card and Bank accounts are linked under one account. 100 of thousands website accept payment through Paypal because of many reasons. Some are as below:
    • Payment is Easy
    • Payment is secure as Payment details are not shared with vendors
    • Buyer can perform shopping without sharing sensitive data with Online Shop
    • No need to add shipping address and payment details each time you shop online
    • Payment details are PayPal purchase protection - Secure
Here are the steps of typical transaction on E-Commerce:
    1. User add the product to the product cart
    2. User finishes the shopping and chooses to checkout
    3. User chooses to checkout with PayPal and logs into the account
    4. User selects preferred payment option linked to his PayPal account
    5. User sees a confirmation page to verify that the purchase is complete
    6. PayPal notifies the seller when the funds have been received
    7. User receives an email from seller confirming that the order is in progress
    121. Payment Gateway - Limitation of PayPal in Pakistan
PayPal has presence in over 190 + countries but unfortunately PayPal gateway does not support payment processing from Pakistan. The business case of payment gateway does not seem to be fit for PayPal in Pakistan due to many reasons which include internet scams hacking and State Bank of Pakistan regulation related to electronic payments. In short, PayPal services are not available in Pakistan.
    122. Payment Gateway in Pakistan - What is EasyPaisa?
EasyPaisa is product of collaboration between Telenor and Tameer Microfinance Bank to transfer money securely, instantly between persons. The money is transferred through 4000 plus outlets across country. EasyPaisa is first End-to-End Online payment solution for Online seller and their customers and it EasyPaisa is first End-to-End Online payment solution for Online seller and their customers. Plugins are available for EasyPaisa to be integrated with Shopping Carts like Magento and Prestashop.
    123. Payment Gateway in Pakistan – EasyPaisa --- How it Work
Easypaisa Solution is an electronic payment solution that enables internet users to make financial transaction online. It can easily and seamlessly be integrated with any online website and/or shopping cart and enable users to pay online through Easypay.
Merchants should register at the EasyPaisa Website to get unique store id which would be used to integrate EasyPaisa plugin into the shopping cart. Customers will choose EasyPay as the payment option.
    125. Payment Gateway in Pakistan – Sandbox Environment
Payment gateways need to be tested before launching because stakes of small mistakes could be very high as it includes financial transaction. Sandbox environment are clone of production i.e. Testing Environment but simulate live gateway environment. Service Provider usually provides Sandbox credentials with dummy data to verify functionality of Gateway. In other words, the services are completely and thoroughly tested with dummy data with the intention of finding any flaws so that they can be eradicated before the services becomes available to end users.     151. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- How to Handle 301's
The concept of 301 is about sending User and Search Engine on different Web Page (URL) from the one they originally requested permanently. Search engine interpret it as new page and updated version of content. Let’s have a look on the images below:

In case of 301, search engine will take weightage of previous page to new page in essence and the page ranking weight will also be carried to the redirected page because, as mentioned above, search engine is assuming that page B is the updated version of page A. It might take some time for Search Engine to discover 301 because crawler might take some time to re-index pages after redirection.
    152. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- How to Handle 404
Error 404 reflects that Server (Apache) is not able to found page requested by client because it could be either be deleted or redirected or due to some internal error. Whatever the reason be, 404 can affect visitor experience drastically. It is highly recommended to have custom ‘404 page’ with proper message to end user to avoid any kind of negative impression. The error usually looks like this:


    153. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- Hyphen vs. Underscores
This is another important area for search engine optimization. URL helps Google to interpret more about Webpage from relevance and content view point. So the recommended practice is to make URL more relevant to contents rather non-elaborative in order to help Google to understand it better. This will help significantly in gaining better SEO results. Further the URL must be using hyphens instead of underscore because it will make it different to understand leading to poor SEO results. Consider the following example in order to understand the importance of relevant contents along with hyphens:
Sample URL: https://www.daraz.pk/mobile-surface-screen-protectors/
URL containing hyphens (–):  It is interpreted as ‘mobile surface screen protectors’, making it easy for Google to understand so better SEO results
URL Containing underscore (_):  if the same URL contains underscore instead of hyphens, it would look like this: https://www.daraz.pk/mobile_surface_screen_protectors/. In such case underscore (_) is interpreted as mobilesurfacescreenprotectors make it hard for Google to understand, so SEO results are impacted.
    154.  Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- Canonicals
Approx. 29% of content on Internet is duplicated, may be unintentional. Same Content with same URL makes it hard for Search Engine to find out which version of content is more relevant / updated to search query. Crawler got confused in identifying and deciding which content to index.  Technically not a penalty but has impact on Page Ranking. The solution to this problem is specifying which version of content is correct / original version. Canonical Tag tells Search Engine which URL is master copy of content.
    155. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- How to Handle Canonicals
For Humans its same result set but for Search Engine all are different. The following three pages are duplicates. The second and third example URLs contains a sort parameter ("? sort=color" or "?sort=price"), which creates only a slight difference between these pages (in the way the products listed are sorted). But these pages would still have the same products, the same images, the same text, and, likely, the same title and description tags:
    • http://www.domain.com/product-list.html
    • http://www.domain.com/product-list.html?sort=color
    • http://www.domain.com/product-list.html?sort=price
The canonical tag needs to be added to each potentially duplicated page. The most common is to use a <link/> element in the <head/> of your web page. Here is an example of the canonical code with the URL in the href attribute.
<link rel="canonical" href="http://www.domain.com/canonical-url" />

    156. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- Keyword Planning and Content Generation
Relevant Words and keyword related to content of any website improve the chance of finding its content among the results. The keywords may include synonyms, relevant words, or the words used in the post or webpage. Google look for these key words in articles to find out relevance. For example: if the theme of a webpage is flower, Related Soil, sun, sunflower, leaves, colors could be relevant keywords.


    157. Search Engine Optimization - Quick Walkthrough --- Keyword Generating Tools
How to generate Keywords for your Website? Let’s understand with the help of example:
Assume: Bikes are planned to be sold on Website:
Put yourself in Shoe of Customer and Brainstorm what your Customer can search on Search Engine, can start with following:
    • Buy Bike – Bike Sales, Cheap Bikes , top bike companies
    • Bike accessories – Helmet, Brakes
    • Questions about Bike – Cost of Honda CD 70, Latest model of Honda CD 70
    • Local Search – Bikes available in Lahore
There are tools available in the market for keyword generation. Few are as under:
    • www.soolvo.com  – Help to Generate Keywords, topic to write article , add keyword to Web Page
    • www.ubersuggest.org  – Generate Keywords by adding Alphabets
    • www.keywordtool.io

    161. The Laws of Project Management --- Rationale for Management
Nikola Tesla invented the way electricity is used today. He envisions and created wireless communication. He has photographic memory but he was bad at Management and Business. Generating Ideas is a great characteristic but execution is 80% and idea is 20% in overall success story; Execution is Management. He died collecting his pension and feeding pigeons because he failed to convince investors to fund his ideas. So the success and scalability of any business lies it in management along with Vision.

    58. Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Active Online Presence
Just like another business, online businesses need to attract customers in order to successful generation of business. So online store businesses must focus on continuous marketing activities while using multiple channels so the customer know about the existence of online store. Not only this, customers should be updated regularly by running different campaigns in order to attract them. Promotions, offers, sales and discounts should be properly communicated to customers constantly and they must be related to customers in order to increase their interest in buying and for that content on store should be updated in real-time.
    59. Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Mobile Responsive Website
Technology not only makes things easy for businesses but add challenges as well. Customers are accessing Desktop and Mobile devices to access online stores, ecommerce store must ensure customers enjoy same user experience regardless of the device. One such thing is responsive website which means website should be open properly without disorientation in Mobile and other devices (tablet). Mobile users are increasing day by day; roughly there are 5 billion mobile users in 2018 as compared to 4.01 billion in 2013. This increase in numbers makes responsive website a key success factor for online businesses. Examples of responsive websites are as follows:
    • www.amazon.com
    • www.aliexpress.com
And the example of non-responsive website is:
    • www.fccollege.edu.pk
    60. Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Guest Sign In
Another important factor is the ease of purchasing a product from an online store because online shopping is about convenience with no-bargain facility. Some store required a hectic procedure to create an account before they can actually checkout with the product. Guest Sign is to enable customer to proceed with online shopping without forcing to register first. According to a research in 2017, “creating an account” was the second biggest reason behind abandoning purchase during checkout followed by “too long and complex checkout process” on third number.

    61. Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Product Catalogue and Branded Products
Customers’ needs information about the product they are interested to purchase. Not only this, they want to see the product online just to increase their level of satisfaction. So it is of utmost importance to create a product && product details page along with add high quality product images in different zoom/angles. In order to support customers in making buying decision, an online store must have:
    • Product description, price, quantity available should be mentioned explicitly
    • Specification of product to be mention with warranty
    • High quality images of the products
    • Shipping details like time and cost etc.
    62. Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Product Review and Rating
Product reviews and rating from previous buyers are another source of convincing a customer to make a purchase decision. Customers may find information about the utility and quality of the product they are interested in and that increase the probability of checkout. Positive reviews will increase the level of trust between the store and customers, which is the biggest challenge in ecommerce, as they give good impression about the product quality, utility, reliability of product and store.
    63.  Online Store: Components of Online Store -- Recommendations

Course Design and student centered learning

Teaching Principles
Teaching is a complex, multifaceted activity, often requiring us as instructors to juggle multiple
tasks and goals simultaneously and flexibly. The following small but powerful set of principles
can make teaching both more effective and more efficient, by helping us create the conditions
that support student learning and minimize the need for revising materials, content, and policies.
While implementing these principles requires a commitment in time and effort, it often saves
time and energy later on.

    1. Effective teaching involves acquiring relevant knowledge about students
       and using that knowledge to inform our course design and classroom
       teaching.

       When we teach, we do not just teach the content, we teach students the content. A variety
       of student characteristics can affect learning. For example, students’ cultural and
       generational backgrounds influence how they see the world; disciplinary backgrounds
       lead students to approach problems in different ways; and students’ prior knowledge
       (both accurate and inaccurate aspects) shapes new learning. Information about these
       characteristics should be used to inform course design,
       to help explain student difficulties and to guide
       instructional adaptations.

    2. Effective teaching involves aligning the three
       major components of instruction: learning
       objectives, assessments, and instructional
       activities.

       Taking the time to do this upfront saves time in the
       end and leads to a better course. Teaching is more
       effective and student learning is enhanced when (a)
       we, as instructors, articulate a clear set of learning objectives (i.e., the knowledge and
       skills that we expect students to demonstrate by the end of a course); (b) the instructional
       activities (e.g., case studies, labs, discussions, readings) support these learning objectives
       by providing goal-oriented practice; and (c) the assessments (e.g., tests, papers, problem
       sets, performances) provide opportunities for students to demonstrate and practice the
       knowledge and skills articulated in the objectives, and for instructors to offer targeted
       feedback that can guide further learning.

    3. Effective teaching involves articulating explicit expectations regarding
       learning objectives and policies.

       There is amazing variation in what is expected of students across American classrooms
       and even within a given discipline. For example, what constitutes evidence may differ
       greatly across courses; what is permissible collaboration in one course could be

Q 2: Define three main temperatures of colors. Explain each type with Examples
Solution:
The three main temperatures of colors are:

* **Warm colors: Red, orange, and yellow. These colors evoke feelings of warmth, excitement, and energy. Examples of warm colors in nature include sunsets, fire, and ripe fruit.
* **Cool colors:** Blue, green, and purple. These colors evoke feelings of calmness, relaxation, and peace. Examples of cool colors in nature include the sky, the ocean, and forests.
* **Neutral colors:** White, black, and gray. These colors are neither warm nor cool. Neutral colors can be used to balance out warm and cool colors in a design.

Here are some additional examples of each type:

**Warm colors:**

* Apricot
* Bronze
* Coral
* Gold
* Maroon
* Peach
* Pink
* Rose
* Salmon
* Sienna
* Terracotta

**Cool colors:**

* Aquamarine
* Azure
* Cobalt
* Cyan
* Emerald
* Indigo
* Lavender
* Navy
* Teal
* Turquoise
* Violet

**Neutral colors:**

* Beige
* Cream
* Dove gray
* Ecru
* Fawn
* Ivory
* Khaki
* Taupe
* Wheat

Artists and designers use color temperature to create different effects in their work. For example, a warm color scheme can be used to create a sense of warmth or intimacy, while a cool color scheme can be used to create a sense of spaciousness or calm. Neutral colors can be used to balance out warm and cool colors, or to create a sense of simplicity or sophistication.

Here are some examples of how color temperature can be used to create different effects:

* **Warm color scheme:** A warm color scheme can be used to create a cozy and inviting atmosphere in a living room. For example, you could paint the walls a warm color like peach or apricot, and then decorate with furniture and accessories in other warm colors, such as red, orange, and yellow.
* **Cool color scheme:** A cool color scheme can be used to create a calming and relaxing atmosphere in a bedroom. For example, you could paint the walls a cool color like blue or green, and then decorate with furniture and accessories in other cool colors, such as purple and silver.
* **Neutral color scheme:** A neutral color scheme can be used to create a sleek and sophisticated look in a kitchen or bathroom. For example, you could paint the walls a neutral color like white or gray, and then decorate with appliances and fixtures in other neutral colors, such as stainless steel or black.

    Arbitrariness :In human language, there is no natural connection between the word and

     based on that of a parent language, although usually with significant pronunciation,
     meaning and grammar differences.
    Derivation :Derivation creates new words with different meanings, e.g. maltreat from
     treat. With different syntactic properties, e.g. the adverb quickly from the adjective quick.

     geographical area. Different dialects are distinguished from each other by their
     vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation (whereas a distinction made only in terms of
     pronunciation is usually called an accent). A dialect of a language is distinguishable, but
     still understandable, to speakers of another dialect of that language.
    Displacement :In linguistics, displacement is the capability of language to communicate
     about things that are not immediately present (spatially or temporally); i.e., things that are
     either not here or are not here now.
    Duality :Human language is organized at two levels or layers simultaneously. We have a
     physical level at which we can produce individual sounds, like n, b and i. As individual
     sounds, none of these discrete forms has any intrinsic meaning. In a particular
     combination such as bin, we have another level producing a meaning that is different
     from the meaning of the combination in nib.Among other creatures, each communicative
     signal appears to be a single fixed form that cannot be broken down into separate
     parts.Your dog may be able to produce woof (“I’m happy to see you”).It does not seem to
     do so on the basis of a distinct level of production combining the separate elements of
     w+oo+f. If the dog was operating with the double level (i.e. duality), then we might
     expect to hear different combinations with different meanings, such as oowf (“I’m
     hungry”) and foow (“I’m really bored”).

ENG(507-512) Glossary

    Advanced tongue root (ATR) :Having the root of the tongue pulled forward so as to
     widen the pharynx (and, often, to raise the body of the tongue nearer to the roof of
     the mouth). Pharyngeal sounds are [-ATR], as the pharynx is narrowed.
    affricate :A stop followed by a homorganic fricative.
    allophone :A variant of a phoneme. The allophones of a phoneme form a set of sounds
     that (1) do not change the meaning of a word, (2) are all very similar to one another,
     and (3) occur in phonetic contexts different from one another—for example,syllable
     initial as opposed to syllable final. The differences between allophones can be stated
     in terms of phonological rules.
    alternations :Variations in words that can be described in terms of phonological rules;
     for example, the difference between [ aI ] and [ I ] in divine, divin(ity).
    alveolar :An articulation involving the tip or blade of the tongue and the alveolar
     ridge, as in English [ d ] in die.
    alveolar ridge :The part of the upper surface of the mouth immediately behind the
     front teeth.
    alveolo-palatal :Post-alveolar consonant produced with significant raising of the front
     of the tongue toward the palate.
    ambisyllabic :Belonging to two syllables. A consonant such as [ p ] in happy is
     sometimes said to be ambisyllabic.
    apical :An articulation involving the tip of the tongue.
    approximant :An articulation in which one articulator is close to another but without
     the tract being narrowed to such an extent that a turbulent airstream is produced. In
     many forms of English, / j, l, r, w / are approximants.
    articulator :One of several parts of the vocal tract that can be used to form speech
     sounds.
    aspiration :A period of voicelessness after the release of an articulation, as in English
     in pie [ pÓaI].
    assimilation :The change of one sound into another making it more similar to a
     neighboring sound, as in the change of underlying [ n ] to [ m ] in input [ ·ImpÁt ] or of
     underlying [ z ] to [ Z ] in does she [ ·dØZSi ].
    back vowel :Vowel in which the body of the tongue is in the back part of the oral
     cavity (mouth). The vowels [ u, o, O, A ] form a set of back reference vowels.
    bilabial :An articulation involving both lips, as in English [ m ] in my.
    binary feature :A feature (for example, Lateral) that can be used to classify sounds in
     terms of two possibilities.

    breathy voice :Another name for murmur; a type of phonation in which the vocal folds
     are only slightly apart so that they vibrate while allowing a high rate of airflow

    broad transcription :A transcription that does not show a great deal of phonetic d
     etail; often a simple phonemic transcription.
    cardinal vowels :A set of reference vowels first defined by Daniel Jones. The vowels
     of any language can be described by stating their relationships to the cardinal vowels.
    citation form :The form a word has when it is cited or pronounced in isolation.
    click :A stop made with an ingressive v elaric airstream, such as Zulu [ = ].
    closed syllable :A syllable with a consonant at the end, as the first syllables in English
     magpie, pantry, completion.
    coarticulation :The overlapping of adjacent articulations.
    coda :The consonants occurring after the vowel in a syllable.
    contour tone :A tone in a language such as Chinese that must be specified as a gliding
     movement within the pitch range.
    coronal :A term for sounds articulated with the tip or blade of the tongue raised
     toward the teeth or the alveolar ridge (or, sometimes, the hard palate), such as [ T, s,
     t ].
    creaky voice :See laryngealization.
    declination :Gradual intonational pitch fall over the course of an utterance.
    dental :Refers to sounds made with the tongue touching the teeth.
    diacritic :Small added mark that can be used to distinguish different values of a
     symbol. For example, the addition of [ º] distinguishes a velarized from a nonvelarized
     sound, as in [ l º ] as opposed to [ l ].
    diphthong :A vowel in which there is a change in quality during a single syllable, as in
     English [ aI 8] in high.
    dorsal :Describing a sound articulated with the back of the tongue.
    dorsum :The back of the tongue.
    downdrift :The tendency for the pitch to fall throughout an intonational phrase.
    ease of articulation :A phonetic force that impacts linguistic sound systems so that
     patterns that are easier to produce are more likely than difficult patterns.
    ejective :A stop made with an egressive glottalic airstream, such as Hausa [ k' ].
    epenthesis :The insertion of one or more sounds in the middle of a word, such as the
     pronunciation of sense as [ s”nts ].
    exemplar theory :The idea that phonetic categories are represented in the mind as a
     set of all of the examples of the category that the speaker has produced and/or heard.
    feature :A phonetic property of a sound. Some features like Coronal are fairly general,
     while others like Laminal Dental are more specific.
    filter :In acoustic phonetics, a filter is an acoustic tube that enhances some frequency
     components of a sound source while decreasing the amplitudes of other components.
    flap :An articulation in which one a rticulator, usually the tongue tip, is drawn back
     and then allowed to strike against another articulator in returning to its rest position.
    formant :A resonating frequency of the air in the vocal tract. Vowels are

ENG (522-524 & 529) Glossary

 applied linguistics
The application of insights from theoretical linguistics to practical matters such as language
teaching, remedial linguistic therapy, language planning or whatever.
 arbitrariness
An essential notion in structural linguistics which denies any necessary relationship between
linguistic signs and their referents, e.g. objects in the outside world.
 areas of linguistics
Any of a number of areas of study in which linguistic insights have been brought to bear, for
instance sociolinguistics in which scholars study society and the way language is used in it. Other
examples are psycholinguistics which is concerned with the psychological and linguistic
development of the child.
 Chronology
Content may be sequenced according to the order in which events occur in the real world. For
example, in a writing course the organization might be based on the sequence writers are assumed
to employ when composing: (1) brainstorming; (2) drafting; (3) revising; (4) editing. In a
proficiency course, skills might be sequenced according to the sequence in which they are nor-
mally acquired: (1) listening; (2) speaking; (3) reading; (4) writing.
 competence
According to Chomsky in his Aspects of the theory of syntax (1965) this is the abstract ability of
an individual to speak the language which he/she has learned as native language in his/her
childhood. The competence of a speaker is unaffected by such factors as nervousness, temporary
loss of memory, speech errors, etc. These latter phenomena are entirely within the domain of
performance which refers to the process of applying one's competence in the act of speaking. Bear
in mind that competence also refers to the ability to judge if a sentence is grammatically well-
formed; it is an unconscious ability.
 context
A term referring to the environment in which an element (sound, word, phrase) occurs. The context
may determine what elements may be present, in which case one says that there are 'co-occurrence
restrictions' for instance 1) /r/ may not occur after /s/ in a syllable in English, e.g. */sri:n/ is not
phonotactically permissible in English; 2) the progressive form cannot occur with stative verbs,
e.g. We are knowing German is not well-formed in English.
